query: In otherwise healthy adults aged 20–65 who use caffeine to support work/academic focus, which dosing strategies—dose (mg/kg), timing relative to wake/sleep and circadian phase, cycling/washout schedules, and co-ingestion specifically with L-theanine—maximize acute cognitive performance (vigilance, reaction time, working memory) while minimizing tolerance, anxiety symptoms, and sleep disruption? How are these strategies characterized across peer-reviewed clinical and performance literature, sports-science evidence, and health-agency guidelines, and which long-term habits (e.g., daily intake caps, “caffeine curfew,” deload weeks, chronotype-based timing) sustain efficacy over ≥3 months? Synthesize global evidence with priority on 2017-2026 trials and meta-analyses, including case reports/series for context; exclude other nootropics/adaptogens unless directly compared with caffeine in randomized studies.
